compare.intro: This unit's points come in look-alike sets: おかげで thanks someone for a good result, せいで blames someone for a bad one, and ため just names the cause in formal Japanese; ため follows a noun with の or a plain-form verb, while によって follows a noun only and sounds like the news; ものだから gives your own reason or excuse, while から and ので give any reason and can also come before an invitation; からこそ says this is the real reason, while のだから points to a fact you both know and leads to advice or an order; わけだ draws a conclusion you have just worked out, わけではない says an idea is not fully true, and はずだ is what you expect but have not checked.

forms.tag: 言いわけ · my own reason, often an excuse
forms.ja: ドアが開いていた{ものだから}、つい中に入ってしまいました。
forms.en: The door was open, so I just walked in.

forms.tag: 知っているでしょう · since we both know it
forms.ja: あなたがさそった{んだから}、[遅|おく]れないで来てね。
forms.en: You're the one who invited us, so don't be late.

forms.tag: それが本当の理由 · precisely because
forms.ja: 小さい店だ{からこそ}、お[客|きゃく]さん一人一人を大切にしています。
forms.en: Precisely because we are a small shop, we look after every customer.

check.label: Saying sorry with your own reason
check.q: すみません、[説明書|せつめいしょ]が^英語だけ^（　　）、使い方がよく分からなくて。
why: んですから points to a fact the listener already knows and leads to advice or a judgement. Here the speaker is telling their own reason in an apology.
The speaker says sorry and gives their own reason: the manual is only in English. ものですから is the polite excuse, and 英語だけ takes な before it.
からこそ stresses that this, and nothing else, is the real reason, to make a point. A simple apology with an excuse does not make that point.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: 姉が車で駅まで^送ってくれた^（　　）、[最終|さいしゅう]電車に間に合いました。
why: せいで blames someone for a bad result. Catching the last train is good news.
My sister drove me, and I made the last train: a good result I am thankful for. くれた shows the thanks too.
んだから points to a fact the listener already knows and leads to advice or a judgement. Here the speaker just reports what happened.
わけではなく says an idea is not true and then corrects it. The sister really did drive, and nothing is corrected.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: 先生が急に[病気|びょうき]になった（　　）、^本日の料理教室はお休みいたします^。
why: によって gives a cause only after a noun. It cannot follow a verb like なった.
おかげで is for a good result. A class being called off is not good news.
からこそ stresses that this is the real, special reason. A notice that simply says why the class is off does not stress it.
ため gives the cause in formal Japanese, the style of a notice like お休みいたします. It follows the plain form なった directly.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^[申|もう]しわけありません^。母から急に電話があった（　　）、[連絡|れんらく]が[遅|おそ]くなりました。
why: An apology with your own reason: ものですから gives the excuse politely.
んですから points to a fact the listener already knows. The listener did not know about the call, and an apology does not use it.
からこそ stresses a reason as the real, special one. It does not give an excuse in an apology.
わけではなく denies an idea and then corrects it. The call really happened, and what follows is not a correction.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: 手紙は月曜日に出したので、もう[届|とど]いている（　　）が、^まだ[返事|へんじ]がありません^。
why: わけです gives a conclusion as something now settled. The speaker has no sign that the letter arrived, so the settled tone does not fit before が、まだ返事がありません.
わけではありません says an idea is not fully true. "It is not that it has arrived, but there is no reply" makes no sense.
はずです is what the speaker expects (it was posted on Monday) but has not checked. The expectation and what has happened do not match, so が follows.
ものですから gives your own reason or excuse. "Because it has arrived, but there is no reply" makes no sense.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.after: 、そのせいで夜は[眠|ねむ]れませんでした。
drill.hint: Which tile joins コーヒーの and gives the good side of the coffee? The bad side comes after, with せいで.
drill.full: コーヒーの{おかげで}[会議中|かいぎちゅう]は[眠|ねむ]くなりませんでしたが、そのせいで夜は[眠|ねむ]れませんでした。
drill.explain: おかげで, 会議中は, 眠く, なりませんでしたが. The coffee did two things: thanks to it (おかげで) I stayed awake in the meeting, a good result; because of it (そのせいで) I could not sleep at night, a bad one. 眠く goes right before なりませんでした.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.before: [当店|とうてん]は[昨日|きのう]の
drill.after: 、しばらくお休みいたします。
drill.hint: Which tile gives the cause of the fire damage, right after a noun? ため comes last, after a plain-form verb.
drill.full: [当店|とうてん]は[昨日|きのう]の火事{によって}やけてしまったため、しばらくお休みいたします。
drill.explain: 火事によって, やけて, しまった, ため. 火事によって gives the cause of the burning, after a noun. ため follows the plain form やけてしまった and gives the cause of the closing, in the polite style of a notice.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: 家族とはなれて暮らしてみた（　　）、家族の大切さが分かった。
exam.explain: からこそ: living apart was the real reason the speaker came to see how much family matters. せいで is for a bad result, and this is a good one. によって gives a cause only after a noun, not after a verb like みた. わけではなく denies an idea and corrects it, which makes no sense here.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: 医者に止められている（　　）、お酒は飲まないほうがいいですよ。
exam.explain: んだから: the listener knows the doctor told them to stop, so the speaker uses that fact for advice (ほうがいいですよ). おかげで and せいで look back on a result, good or bad, and do not lead to advice. によって gives a cause only after a noun, not after a verb like いる.

exam.label: Build the sentence
exam.after: 、もう少し広い部屋に引っ越したい。
exam.full: 今の部屋に不満が{ある}わけではないけれど、もう少し広い部屋に引っ越したい。
exam.explain: 不満が, ある, わけでは, ないけれど. 部屋に不満がある is the idea, and わけではない says it is not really true: I am not unhappy with my flat, but I would like a bigger one.

scene.en: A lost-luggage report form at the airport
scene.intro: Tap each word on the form you fill in when your suitcase does not come out at the airport.

words.gloss: to check in, leave in someone's care

check.label: How the exam asks it
check.q: この用紙に、お名前とご住所を（　　）してください。
check.explain: 記入 is writing information into a form, so 用紙に…記入してください fits. 記念 is a keepsake or remembering an occasion, 用意 is getting something ready, and 注文 is ordering; none of them is done to a form with に.

skill.ask: Which rules on the notice apply to Wang, and what must Wang do now?
skill.passage:
手荷物を受け取れなかったお客様へ
①空港の手荷物カウンターで届け出用紙に記入し、^荷物を預けたときにお渡しした引換証といっしょに出してください^。
②見つかった荷物は、ご自宅かホテルまで無料でお届けします。^空港で受け取りたい方だけ^、用紙の「受け取り方法」のところに「空港」と書いてください。
③荷物が見つかるまでの間に、下着や歯ブラシなど、どうしても必要な物を買った場合は、一日五千円までお支払いします。レシートは、^荷物を受け取ったあとで^、下の住所に送ってください。
④^カメラやパソコンなど高い物が入っている方^は、用紙の「内容」のところに、^品物の名前とだいたいの値段^を書いてください。
skill.strategy: Check Wang against each rule in turn: where she wants the bag sent, what is inside it, and whether she has bought anything yet.

item.q: ワンさんは今、空港で届け出用紙に記入している。荷物の中には仕事で使うパソコンが入っている。荷物はホテルに届けてもらいたい。ホテルに着いたら、歯ブラシを買うつもりだ。ワンさんが今しなければならないことはどれか。
options: 引換証を出して、「受け取り方法」のところに「空港」と書く。
歯ブラシのレシートを、引換証といっしょに出す。
引換証を出して、「内容」のところにパソコンの名前とだいたいの値段を書く。
「内容」のところに、歯ブラシの名前と値段を書く。
short: 引換証、パソコンを書く
item.explain: Rule ① says everyone hands in the claim tag with the form. Rule ④ applies because there is a computer in the bag: write its name and rough price under 「内容」. Wang wants the bag sent to her hotel, so she writes nothing under 「受け取り方法」 (rule ②).
why: Only people who want to collect the bag at the airport write 「空港」 (rule ②). Wang wants it sent to her hotel.
Wang has not bought the toothbrush yet, and receipts are sent after the bag arrives, not handed in now (rule ③).
「内容」 is for expensive things in the bag, like the computer (rule ④). A toothbrush she will buy later does not go there.
